name: Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae
description: Along the Nile in southern Egypt, this string of ancient temples includes Abu Simbel, where colossal figures of Ramesses II stare out from a cliff carved in the 13th century BC, and the island sanctuary of Isis at Philae. When Lake Nasser threatened to drown them, the temples were moved to higher ground in a worldwide rescue effort lasting two decades.
